namespace Erdos478

/--
Let $p$ be a prime and $$A_p = \{ k! \pmod{p} : 1\leq k<p\}.$$ Is it true that $$\lvert A_p\rvert \sim (1-\tfrac{1}{e})p?$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_478 : answer(sorry) ↔
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun p : ℕ =>
        (((Finset.Ico 1 p).image (fun k => Nat.factorial k % p)).card : ℝ) / p)
      (Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {p : ℕ | p.Prime})
      (nhds (1 - 1 / Real.exp 1)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos478

reformulations.difference: The source's asymptotic |A_p| ∼ (1−1/e)p is expressed as convergence of |A_p|/p to 1−1/e, with convergence through primes represented by atTop ⊓ principal {p | p.Prime}.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The filter means precisely that each required bound holds for every sufficiently large prime, and it is nontrivial by infinitude of primes. Setting c = 1−1/exp(1), we have c > 0 and p ≠ 0 on primes. Thus |A_p|/p → c iff |A_p|/(c·p) → 1, exactly asymptotic equivalence. Both the filter's epsilon–N interpretation and the asymptotic-equivalence biconditional were proved in the scratch file without using the conjecture.
